questions.question_text: Describe Rama Natha's transformation in 'A Bottle of Dew'. How did Sage Mahipati guide him from laziness to self-reliance?
questions.model_answer: Initially, Rama Natha was a lazy, gullible landowner who neglected his ancestral fields while chasing a gold-making magic potion. Sage Mahipati cleverly instructed him to collect five litres of winter morning dew from banana trees planted by his own hands. Over six years, Rama Natha worked tirelessly to build a massive plantation. When the dew failed to turn copper into gold, the sage displayed gold coins earned by Madhumati from selling the harvested bananas. Realizing that honest labor was the true source of wealth, Rama Natha became a dedicated farmer.
value_points: Initial state: lazy, gullible, neglecting land for potion
Sage's strategy: 6 years of self-planted banana farming and dew gathering
Climax: copper doesn't transform, but banana sales yield real gold coins
Transformation: respecting physical labor and self-reliance

questions.question_text: Write a reflective paragraph (60-80 words) on 'Hard Work vs Shortcuts to Success' based on the themes of 'A Bottle of Dew'.
questions.model_answer: Many people seek shortcuts to wealth, but true success comes only through dedicated effort. In 'A Bottle of Dew', Rama Natha wasted time and fortune seeking a magic potion until Sage Mahipati redirected him to farming. Through six years of systematic labor, he built a prosperous plantation. Real success requires patience, discipline, and persistent work; shortcuts lead to delusion and loss, whereas honest labor brings lasting financial independence and self-respect.
value_points: Contrast between magical shortcuts and physical effort
Citing Rama Natha's six-year plantation experience
Emphasis on patience, discipline, and self-reliance
Concluding statement on dignity of labor

questions.question_text: Analyze the key themes and character/narrative development in 'The Raven and the Fox'.
model_answer: How does Jean de la Fontaine highlight the theme of vanity in 'The Raven and the Fox'?

The poet depicts Mr. Raven holding a valuable morsel of food. Rather than enjoying his meal quietly, his desire for admiration makes him vulnerable. When Reynard the Fox lavishes fake praise on his plumage and sweet voice, the Raven succumbs completely. Eager to prove his artistic greatness and be hailed 'King of the Woods', he opens his beak, causing the morsel to drop. The fable vividly shows how vanity blinds reason.

questions.question_text: Write a structured reflective paragraph (60-80 words) based on the core lesson of 'The Raven and the Fox'.
model_answer: Write a short paragraph on 'Why We Should Beware of Flattery' based on the poem.

Flattery is insincere praise used to manipulate others for personal gain. Unlike honest appreciation, flatterers appeal to our vanity to weaken our judgment. As shown in 'The Raven and the Fox', accepting false compliments can lead to embarrassing losses. We must cultivate self-awareness and remain cautious when showered with exaggerated praise.
